subject: math
verificationNotes: Hand-authored; numeric answers checked with sympy.
intro: Quantitative data are numeric measurements. Common displays are dotplots, stemplots, and histograms (which group values into bins). Describe a distribution by its shape (symmetric, skewed left, or skewed right), center, spread, and any outliers. Skewness points toward the longer tail: a right-skewed distribution has a tail of large values pulling the mean above the median.

items.prompt: A histogram of incomes has a long tail toward high values. Describe the skew and compare mean to median.

steps: A long tail on the high (right) side means the distribution is skewed right.
The few large values pull the mean upward more than the median.
So the mean is greater than the median for right-skewed data.

items.prompt: Data: $2,3,3,4,5,5,5,6,7$. Make a stemplot description and state the mode.

steps: All values are single digits, so one stem '0' holds leaves $2,3,3,4,5,5,5,6,7$.
The most frequent value (the mode) is $5$ (appears three times).

items.prompt: In a histogram with bin width $10$ starting at $0$, a value of $25$ falls in which bin?
A test-score histogram has a tail toward low values. What skew?

steps: Tail on the low (left) side means skewed left.

items.prompt: For symmetric data, how do mean and median compare?
Value $17$ in bins of width $5$ from $0$: which bin?
